findings.where: Nav bar logo (MMM INFRA lockup, top left) and the hero drawing, at both widths
findings.fault: The logo appears only in white. The wordmark has lost its fixed logo blue and the arches their logo grey. The hero blows the mark up and paints an amber hatch into its third arch. No white version is held, and the logo blue would not reach 3:1 on this diazo ground. As drawn, this direction cannot use the real logo anywhere on its own ground.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who keeps the logo and wants it built by the opening animation. The founder, because a reversed or altered mark needs the client's yes. Choosing v2 would quietly commit Mark to a logo version he has not approved.

findings.where: The page as a whole: hero, article specimen and texture
findings.fault: The tile never shows a photograph or a video frame on the blueprint ground. There is no slot for Mark's portrait and no picture in the article specimen. Nothing shows how a real photo, such as a LinkedIn image Angélique adds to a post, sits in this look. Mark is heard in the article but never seen.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who wants to be seen, wants the images refreshed and welcomes video. Angélique, who will add pictures with posts and has no model for how they should sit on blue linework. A development-bank visitor, who looks for the real person before writing.

findings.where: Hero, first screen, against the motion sketch
findings.fault: The name, the pitch and the Write to Mark button are on screen from the first frame. Only the cut and the amber light animate in. So the picture-first, words-later principle the direction rests on is never shown.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose calm-first value (one quiet moving picture before any text asks for anything) is the reason this direction exists. The animation round, which has no timing for the words to follow.

findings.where: Hero drawing, the amber hatched third bay, against the amber Write to Mark button
findings.fault: The primary action's colour is also used for decoration. The hatched bay is the brightest, busiest mark on the first screen and wins the squint over the button. Amber therefore stops meaning 'the one thing to press'.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor scanning for what to do next, whose eye lands on the drawing's amber before the button. The house rule reserves the primary action's colour. This goes to the founder as a clash with the card's 'amber marks the live part'.

findings.where: Article specimen body and quote, motion-sketch table and notes, palette notes, at both widths
findings.fault: The full 20 mm and 100 mm grid runs unbroken behind running prose and table text. Lines cross every line of an article, so a long read sits on a busy ground.
findings.who_objects: A reader working through one of Mark's long articles (Read mode). Mark, who rejects busyness. Every post Angélique adds would inherit the noise.

findings.where: Hero, the caption under the name (INFRASTRUCTURE ADVISOR / LONGITUDINAL SECTION A-A • SCALE NTS) and the circled 'A'
findings.fault: Mark's role is set in the same small spaced capitals, at the same weight, as drawing jargon, which sits directly under it. In the five-second read, 'Infrastructure advisor' competes with 'longitudinal section A-A' and 'NTS'. The circled 'A' beside the name reads as an initial badge or avatar, not a section marker.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank staffer arriving from LinkedIn, who needs who and what at a glance and gets an engineer's labels instead. Mark, whose voice is a personal advisor, not an engineering sheet.

findings.where: Hero, Write to Mark button, and the nav and title block, as the only contact routes
findings.fault: The only working contact is a mailto: link behind a button. The email address never appears as text, and the nav's CONTACT goes nowhere (#).
findings.who_objects: A visitor on webmail or a locked-down agency machine, where mailto: opens nothing or the wrong client, who then cannot find the address to copy.

findings.where: Nav bar: PROFILE, ARTICLES, BLOG, CONTACT, and the logo home link
findings.fault: Every nav link goes to '#', so the nav bar does nothing when clicked.
findings.who_objects: A visitor trying the tile's nav to reach Mark's profile or articles.

findings.where: Nav bar and title block strip (DRAWING MMM-GA-001, SCALE NTS)
findings.fault: The static drawing-number and scale cells sit in the same ruled cells, light on blue in spaced capitals, as the four nav links. One strip mixes clickable links with data that does nothing.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who clicks MMM-GA-001 expecting a page, or cannot tell where the nav ends.

findings.fault: A button that acts in place is styled like a link: underlined text, with no fill or edge. It borrows the link's signifier.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who expects an underlined phrase to take them somewhere and is surprised when the drawing replays instead.

findings.where: Article specimen, the boxed lecture item (Streamlining the PPP Process…)
findings.fault: The whole box looks like one card target, but only the underlined title acts. The meta line and the box's empty area do nothing.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who clicks the box or the 'PDF' label and gets nothing.

findings.where: Hero drawing, the thin curve rising off the right end of the ground line
findings.fault: A stray curve with no label rises beside the aqueduct. It is not a dimension, a section line or part of the structure, so it reads as a drawing error.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who reads it as an unexplained mark on an otherwise exact sheet, and an engineer-minded viewer for whom it breaks the drawing's logic.

findings.where: Article specimen title, and the article and lecture dates
findings.fault: The type pair says headings are ExtraBold capitals, but the article title is in mixed case. The post's date reads '18 September 2024' in text type, while the lecture's reads '2026-04-23' in mono. Like parts are treated differently on one page.
findings.who_objects: The layout round and Angélique, who get two answers for how a heading and a date should look when adding a post.

findings.fault: The hatch and poche swatches run flush to the panel edges, the EARTH HATCH label touches the frame, and the dimension line has become an empty ruled strip under them. The specimen looks broken.
findings.who_objects: Mark, viewing the tile on a phone, who sees an unfinished panel in the texture the direction is built on.
